$comment: Access control x dispatch. Every above-ground floor sits inside an access zone, so the dispatcher's eligibility filter must intersect service zoning (which shafts reach the floor) with access zoning (which credentials may reach it) on every single call. The executive floor is reachable by exactly one bank and exactly two credential groups.
name: Secure Tower
notes: Access zoning is the point of this building, not decoration: only the lobby is unrestricted. Every other floor belongs to exactly one zone, so no call can be scored without an access check, and a naive dispatcher that filters on servesFloors alone will assign cars to trips the passenger may not legally take.

The executive floor deliberately excludes the 'facilities' and 'security' groups that every tenant zone grants. There is no universal credential, so an implementation cannot short-circuit the check with a building-wide allow-list.

FLOOR 30 IS CREDENTIAL-ISOLATED AND THAT IS A KNOWN, MEASURED DEFECT WHICH IS NOT FIXED HERE. 'exec' and 'exec-escort' appear in no zone but 'executive', while floors 2-29 are all zoned, so credentialForRoute returns null for every route joining 30 to any other restricted floor: 56 origin-destination pairs are dropped, floor 30's whole 10% interfloor share is orphaned and redistributed into outgoing, and its 12 occupants can reach the lobby and nowhere else. It is honest - the loader says so in a warning naming the floor and the rate - but it is not what a secure tower means, and it means the interfloor slider moves nothing for this floor's riders. Every dispatcher, template, traffic profile and seed carries it.

THE FIX WAS BUILT AND MEASURED AND THEN DELIBERATELY NOT APPLIED, and the reason is the cost rather than the fix. One credential group - 'exec' appended LAST to tenant-delta's credentialGroups, floor 30 being Delta's executive suite - clears it: the Floor "30" warning goes away, dropped pairs go 56 to 42 (the 42 that remain are cross-tenant trips, which access control is FOR), and access refusals are unmoved and non-zero at 7 / 7 / 11 for seeds 20260810-12, so the gate still bites (DECISIONS.md § D265, § D266). Measured on the legs at seed 20260810 under eta over a 7200 s window at 30% of population per 5 min, legs leaving 30 go from 6 outgoing / 0 interfloor to 3 / 3 and legs arriving from 33 / 0 to 33 / 1; at the DEFAULT 1800 s window the seeds 20260810-29 producing at least one non-lobby leg touching floor 30 go from 0 of 20 to 8 of 20. It must be appended last, not first: credentialForRoute returns the first group in declared order that covers the route and the credential gap hands a rider starting inside a zone that zone's own first group, so 'exec' first would re-label every intra-delta trip and every delta resident's badge. WHAT IT COSTS, which is why it is not in: secure-tower is what benchmark/accessControl.ts measures, so the one line moves 14 pinned figures in packages/experiments/src/benchmark/published.ts - including the headline difference-of-differences, +1.020 [+0.625, +1.414] to +1.003 [+0.608, +1.398] - plus four coverage rows, the kiosk column, and data/scenario-goals.json's stage-5-credentials counts. That headline is quoted in seven prose documents and guarded four ways by experiments/src/validation/documentation.test.ts. It also fails 18 assertions across 8 test files in 4 packages, four of which (traffic/generator.test.ts, at lines 329, 335, 361 and 1111) exist to PIN this isolation and would have to be rehomed onto a synthetic fixture. Landing it is a re-pinning exercise with a decision record, not a data edit.

'exec-escort' is declared and unreachable, and it is recorded rather than deleted. credentialForRoute returns the FIRST group of the route's first restricted floor that covers the whole route, and the executive zone lists exec before exec-escort while exec-escort appears in no zone exec does not - so no route can resolve to it, and the credential gap hands a floor-30 rider 'exec' for the same reason. Making it reachable would mean giving the ESCORT more reach than the executive, which is backwards; deleting it would remove the only declaration in this file that an escorted visit is a distinct credential. It is a name the data carries and the generator cannot return, which is the data-side twin of the dead-seam rule in CLAUDE.md, and it is stated here so a reader does not infer from its presence that escorted visits are being simulated.

This building is the ONLY SHIPPED WITNESS for traffic/generator.ts's orphaned-share branch - the one that redistributes a demand share which has lost every candidate destination instead of deleting it and quietly running the building below the rate its profiles specify. That is a second thing connecting floor 30 costs, and it is a real one: after the fix above, no building in data/buildings/ orphans a share, so traffic/generator.test.ts's 'does not lose the interfloor share of a credential-isolated floor' would need a fixture of its own. It is not an argument for leaving the defect - a branch nothing shipped reaches is still reachable by any zoning a player authors - but whoever applies the fix has to build that fixture in the same commit.

Tenant zones do not align with bank boundaries by accident: alpha (2-8) and bravo (9-15) are low-bank only, charlie (16-22) and delta (23-29) plus executive (30) are high-bank only. An interfloor trip such as 6 -> 18 is legal by credential only for holders of both tenant groups, and is physically impossible without a lobby transfer regardless. The eligibility filter is the intersection of service zoning and access zoning, never either one alone.

G is the only floor served by both banks, so it is flagged isTransferFloor as well as isEntrance. Every interfloor journey that crosses the low/high boundary changes cars there - 6 -> 18 is low bank 6 -> G, then high bank G -> 18 - and without the flag the first leg would terminate at G instead of joining the second, so time-to-destination would be wrong for exactly the trips this building exists to make awkward. Ground lobbies are not implicitly transfer-capable: the flag is declared here, in mixed-use-high-rise and in vertical-city rather than inferred from isEntrance.

Occupancy is deliberately low-density (26-44 per floor; secure floor plates run 18-20 m2 per person). Each bank is sized to roughly 85% of its up-peak handling capacity under office-standard (12% of population per 5 min): low bank 546 occupants against ~3 cars x 16 design passengers, high bank 446. Switching trafficProfile to office-prestige (16%) pushes both banks past capacity and should trip the saturation flag rather than produce an AWT confidence interval.

4 m/s over a 114.6 m rise is faster than a 30-storey tower strictly needs. That is intentional: adjacent-floor hops of 3.9 m never come close to rated speed, so this building is a second check on the jerk-limited motion profile alongside Garden Apartments.
